reviews.review:
Let's start out with saying Captain Titus is a badass and he'd still be a badass even if he never was a Space Marine. But lucky for us, he is! So that means Badassius Titanius gets to play with toys that are too brutal for videogames. F*ck that, this is Space Marine, even if it's the Ultrasmurfs.

Jokes aside, Single Player pits you in the skin of Captain Titus. The story is a bit predictable, the Orcs are attacking, but you don't really care anyway. This is Space Marine and you have a duty to do. Which is to brutally slaughter Orcs in the most gratuitous way, largely. I won't spoil who the secret enemies are who will start attacking you late-game. (CHAOS MARINES SHHHHH)

Health packs are for Heretics. You regain health by stunning an enemy and using a finisher on them.

You can carry four firearms, whereof two can be swapped out as you so desire. The array of firearms is classical, with every typical playstyle covered sooner or later. The weapons rarely feel underpowered, but you do have a sense of "wrong place, wrong weapon" at times, which urges you to keep a weapon variation based on distances. Something for close, something for far.

Three melee weapons, whereof the Hammer limits your firearm usage to your sidearm or bolter.
Melee feels strong and satisfying. Whenever enemies get close, you'll feel like you can rely on melee to finish them off relatively easily. Using the hammer makes you prone to rush in and tear them up, a tactic better fitting with Orcs or equipped with a Jetpack (which is only available on specific areas, sadly)

If anything, Single Player makes for a great tutorial on how to handle Multiplayer, which is pretty unforgiving.
Multiplayer is pretty much how you imagine Space Marines going at it. It's big, it's harsh and a little bit quick, as your health does not match that of Titus.

All the weapons you encountered in the Singleplayer are present, and an extra melee weapon if you bother to buy it's DLC for it. The way you go about choosing weaponry is unusual and interesting.

You start out with just one class. Which is the classic Bolter. BUT, you can copy the weapon loadout of the person who killed you. No requirements. If you got killed by a guy with a jetpack, copy it and get some payback. Respawning is fast too.
This balances out with being only possible once. Dying again only makes you able to copy that killer's loadout, or pick a class.

Reaching level 4, you'll unlock two things.
First, a customization slot, allowing you to put together your own class type(normal, heavy or jetpacky) with the unlocked weapons available to that class type. Then you can read up on the weapon specs and the available (locked or unlocked) perks a class can have. They are various, and many complement a different playstyle with the same class. Variety is endless, and I'm sure that, having unlocked enough over time, you can cater to your own playstyle.

Secondly, you can customize your Space and Chaos Marine.
Meaning, you can swap out unlocked armor pieces and color your Space Bad*ss in any way you like. In general, the armor has a primary color for the brunt of it, and a secondary such as for trimming and extremities.

The color availability itself is pretty impressive and funnily applicable. Imagine picking colors for a car in GTA or Saints Row, that's the kind of options you get to deal with. You get Reds, Yellows, Blues, Greens, then Metallic's and all that jazz. It's pretty hilarious how your Space Marine suddenly is painted like a car.

You can also choose the emblem that'll appear on your left shoulder armor. But if you are thinking of coloring your Space Marine in honor of a known existing Space Marine chapter, you shouldn't bother putting in the work. These color schemes are readily available for both Space and Chaos Marines, at no cost or unlocking requirement. Including their emblem.

If you like 3rd person shooters with an emphasis on badassery and without sissy features like crouching or cover-based shooting, then Warhammer 40k Space Marine is right up your alley.
Epic game! Must-have for all [i][b]WH40k[/b][/i] fans!
It's British Gears of War. And that is alllll you need to know. :D
